text.p: Roland Europe, the Italian-based maker of electronic musical instruments, said it posted 1996 net profit of 12.72 billion lire, up 77.9 percent on 1995's 7.15 billion.

The company said in a statement after a board meeting to approve the results that sales were 1.5 percent down on 1995 at 107.8 billion lire, due to a depreciation in the Ecu used to invoice most of sales.
In Ecu terms, 1996 sales rose seven percent, it said.

The company, controlled by the Roland Corp of Japan, proposed paying an unchanged ordinary dividend of 200 lire per share and an extraordinary dividend of 100 lire per share to celebrate the company's first 20 years of operations.
Gross operating profit rose 31.7 percent to 18.5 billion lire and net rose 32.8 percent to 15.02 billion.
Net assets were 56.14 billion lire against 26.13 billion.
Quoted on the Milan bourse since June 1996, Roland shares closed 0.56 percent down on Monday at 5,160 lire.
